title: Five-step storytelling framework for viral videos
one_liner: A five-part structure for making storytelling videos more engaging and memorable.
key_points: Hook: state a specific goal and conflict.
Click confirmation: show rising action and progress toward the goal.
Use B-roll to show effort, emotion, and difficulty.
Add a second conflict or down moment halfway through.

hook.text: Copy one of the most famous Hollywood storytelling techniques, and it got me 50 million views and 100,000 followers.

why_saved_guess: The user likely saved this to copy a proven storytelling structure for their own short-form videos.
actionable_takeaways: Map your next video into hook, rising action, setback, climax, and resolution.
Write hooks that include both a goal and a conflict.
Insert a midpoint setback to avoid a straight-line narrative.
remix_idea: Turn this into a niche-specific storytelling template for your audience, using your own goal-conflict-setback-climax examples.
summary: Mino Lee breaks down a five-step storytelling framework he uses in his own videos. The structure is: a hook with a specific goal and conflict, a click confirmation or rising action, a second conflict halfway through, a climactic moment with music, and a resolution that feels earned. He says this approach creates an emotional roller coaster that keeps viewers watching and makes the creator more memorable.

author: jan_amit
title: Taste-skill gap and how to close it
one_liner: A creative framework for turning strong taste into skill through volume, deadlines, and frustration.
key_points: Taste develops through consuming films, music, and art and learning what you recognize as good.
Creation feels bad at first because your skill cannot yet match your taste.
The gap is dangerous when frustration turns into stopping altogether.
Make a lot of work and avoid chasing perfection.

hook.text: There's a reason why you don't like what you do: it's called the taste-skill gap.

why_saved_guess: You wanted a reminder that feeling bad about your early work is normal and that repetition is the way through it.
actionable_takeaways: Make more finished pieces instead of polishing one forever.
Set external deadlines for your next project.
Treat frustration as feedback, not failure.
remix_idea: Make a short reel explaining a creative gap in your niche and give 3 ways to close it.
summary: The post explains the “taste-skill gap”: people often develop strong judgment faster than they develop the ability to make work that matches it. It argues that this gap is normal and can be closed by making lots of work, setting deadlines, and using frustration as proof of growth. The message is to keep taste as a guide, but keep creating until skill catches up.

author: 101xfounders
title: Y Combinator’s founder sales principles
one_liner: Founders should sell by understanding customers, solving real problems, and being useful consistently.
key_points: Keep sales simple: don’t overcomplicate it; just start selling.
Sales is about people and problem-solving, not technology or code.
People buy for four things: time, money, sex, and approval/peace of mind.
People buy aspirin always; vitamins only occasionally and unpredictably.

hook.text: Yes, there are tons of resources but I'll try to offer some simple tips.

why_saved_guess: To remember a practical founder-first approach to selling and customer understanding.
actionable_takeaways: Talk to customers regularly before building a sales team.
Frame your offer around a real problem, not your product features.
Find ways to be useful to people without asking for anything back.
remix_idea: Turn this into a carousel on your niche: replace sales with your customer problem and list 5 founder lessons.
summary: This carousel summarizes Y Combinator-style advice on how founders should approach sales. It argues that early-stage founders are often the first salesperson and should focus on talking to customers, listening more than pitching, and solving a problem people genuinely care about. The slides also list a few sales heuristics: keep it simple, sell to real human needs, be useful, build relationships, and ignore internal metrics when thinking about what customers want.
quotes: Yes, there are tons of resources but I'll try to offer some simple tips.
